question: Can the perceptibility-property itself be perceptible?
premises: if the so-called perceptibility is itself unperceived, it is a sky-flower
if it exists as something perceived, perceptibility applies to it too
that opens an infinite regress of perceptibilities
inference: Reifying perceptibility as a separate property self-destructs.
uncertainties: anavasthiti regress target kept as stated, not resolved
plain_english: But if that so-called perceptibility-property is itself unperceived, it is like a sky-flower; if it exists as perceived, there too is regress upon perceptibility.
